topic.title: Compatibility of task conditioning and linear-moment representation
topic.question: Under the frozen inputs and training protocol, can the g3 task-conditioning approach improve four-task macro ROC-AUC over the stronger g0 linear-moment source at justified parameter and measured compute cost?
topic.hypothesis: The source approaches may preserve complementary predictive information, but redundancy or task interference may erase the smaller task-conditioning gain. Inherit the two committed source approaches, subject to implementation inspection in the next phase; test their combination against both frozen source bests, especially g0 at 0.8283262734957326. Cross representation replacement with task-conditioning removal, retain the available gradient-stop contrasts, and compare capacity and equal training exposure while measuring training/inference cost. Added utility predicts a repeat-confirmed macro-AUC improvement over both sources beyond capacity controls. Failure to exceed g0, equivalent gains from capacity alone, or disappearance under replacement controls opposes complementary utility; unchanged stop contrasts would leave gradient isolation unsupported. Report every task AUC/logloss trade-off. Reserve resources for attribution and repeat confirmation; freeze selection and comparison suite before one withheld assessment. No mechanism or novelty is established by the present summaries.
